title: People Ops - self notes and manager prep (mid-year)
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for mid-year check-in prep, capture wins, examples, metrics, and manager asks. Keep raw - will refine into official self-review doc later.

Context / role highlights (last 6-9 months):
- Lead HRBP for Engineering org (~150 people). Focused on comp cycles, onboarding revamp, manager training, and early ops for Dedicated product launch.
- Took point on cross-functional hiring plan for infra/serving-runtime: partnered with eng managers and recruiting to accelerate pipeline.
- Ran first pilot of the new onboarding checklist + buddy program for private-deployments hires (4 cohorts).

Key accomplishments (impact + metrics):
1) Onboarding revamp:
   - Reduced average new-hire time-to-1st-pr by ~20% (baseline ~7d -> now ~5.5d) - tracked via onboarding survey and GitHub first-commit timestamps.
   - Pilot feedback: 8/10 satisfaction (n=18). Saved ~10 hours/manager onboarding time per hire via standardized checklist and buddy assignments.

2) Hiring & pipeline stabilization for serving-runtime team:
   - Helped hiring managers fill 6 priority IC roles in Q4-Q1 (target was 4) - reduced time-to-offer by ~15%.
   - Implemented scorecard + structured interview rubric for infra roles; improved interviewer calibration (fewer post-offer rejections).

3) Manager training series (M1-M2 fundamentals):
   - Launched 6-session cohort, 48 managers attended. Post-training pulse: +0.4 on manager confidence scale. Early signs of better 1:1 structure in follow-ups.

4) Comp & leveling support for Dedicated customers team:
   - Worked with total comp to build promotion case templates and mapping for new role bands. Reduced review time for promotion packets by ~30%.

Concrete examples to surface in self-review (behavioral + results):
- Example: When the infra hiring funnel slowed (Jan), ran a 2-week blitz: re-prioritized job descriptions, added targeted sourcing channels, re-engaged dormant candidates -> closed 2 critical roles in 3 weeks. Demonstrates bias for action + stakeholder alignment.
- Example: Manager training cohort: collected manager anecdotes showing improved feedback frequency; shared 3 manager testimonials with L&D to iterate content. Shows partnership and measurable adoption.

Strengths (top 3):
- Cross-functional influence: comfortable driving decisions without formal authority (recruiting, eng, product).
- Operational rigor: I turn fuzzy problems into repeatable processes (onboarding checklist, promotion templates).
- Data-informed: use quantitative signals (time-to-offer, survey NPS, commit timestamps) to define impact.

Areas for growth (top 3):
- Strategic prioritization at org-level: I sometimes get deep into execution and need to delegate earlier; goal to delegate more and focus on org strategy.
- Talent development: want to build a sustainable leadership pipeline program (longer-term project).
- Cross-regional HR ops: less experience in APAC-specific compliance and benefits - plan to shadow PMM/legal on next Private deployment sale.

Objectives for next cycle (measurable where possible):
- Objective 1: Reduce time-to-offer for infra/serving-runtime roles by another 10% (baseline current). Key results: standardized scorecards adopted by 90% of interviewers; resources for hiring managers (1-pager) completed.
- Objective 2: Scale onboarding to Dedicated + Private hires: create a launch kit and SRE-specific onboarding path; target new-hire satisfaction >= 8.5/10.
- Objective 3: Pilot leadership development track for senior ICs (IC3+): run one cohort (8 people) and measure promotion readiness at 6 months.

Manager asks / calibration questions for mid-year convo:
- Ask: Guidance on prioritization - which of the onboarding vs hiring funnel vs manager training should I deprioritize if bandwidth constrained? (My current instinct: keep hiring + onboarding, deprioritize running additional manager cohorts until Q3.)
- Ask: Support for delegation - can you help me identify a direct report or peer to offload cohort logistics?
- Ask: Career trajectory - I'm aiming for Sr. Manager, People Ops in the next 12-18 months. Looking for concrete signals: what outcomes would you expect (scope, headcount, program ownership)?
- Calibration: how does my impact compare to other HRBPs cross-company? Any gaps I should be aware of for promotion cycle?

Risks / open questions (notes to self):
- Capacity risk: recruiting team bandwidth predicted to tighten in Q2; need contingency for high-priority role hiring.
- Measurement gaps: commit timestamp approach is noisy for repos where infra folks don't always push public PRs - need alternate onboarding signals (first ticket, internal wiki edit).
- Compliance: Private deployment hires may need specific background checks; confirm process with legal.

Misc TODOs (short checklist):
- [ ] Draft condensed self-review doc for performance system (due 2026-02-25)
- [ ] Create one-pager for hiring managers on structured interviews (due 2026-03-05)
- [ ] Follow up with Alex on promotion template feedback (blocking: comp sign-off)
- [ ] Sync with legal on Private-region hiring checklist (by end of Feb)

Notes for calibration conversation with manager (bulleted script):
- Quick opening: 1-2 min summary of focus areas and top impact metrics.
- Evidence: 2 concrete stories (hiring blitz + onboarding metric).
- Ask for: prioritization guidance, delegation support, promotion criteria.
- Close with: 1-2 commitments for next 90 days and ask for feedback cadence.

Random thoughts / experiments to try (brainstorm):
- Micro-onboarding playbooks embedded in Slack (automated checklist pings).
- Office hours for managers + 15-min rapid interview calibration sessions.
- Mini-study: correlation between manager 1:1 frequency and new-hire ramp time (0.5-1 month analysis).

Links / artifacts I will attach to final self-review:
- onboarding-pilot-feedback-survey (Confluence)
- hiring-scorecard-template (Google Doc)
- manager-training-post-pulse (sheet)
- promotion-template-final (shared drive)

Final quick reflection:
- I'm proud of moving operational projects to stable, repeatable processes that scale. Biggest gap is stepping up to a more strategic partner cadence and delegating operational work earlier. Need manager's help on delegation and clarity on promotion signals.

(End of notes - raw, will edit into formal self-review doc.)
